body.en:
Question B-006-008-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Lower resonant frequency requires greater electrical length, so lengthening the antenna moves its resonance downward.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "shorten it": Shortening the antenna raises its resonant frequency, so it would move the tuning in the wrong direction.
- sourceIndex 2: "use smaller diameter wire": Thinner wire tends to raise resonance slightly and narrow bandwidth, so it moves opposite to the desired lower resonant frequency; lengthening is the proper adjustment.
- sourceIndex 3: "lengthen the transmission line": Changing transmission-line length can change the impedance seen at the shack, but it does not change the antenna element’s actual resonant frequency.
